task_text: Extend this existing SVG board renderer with a user-selected fill color. Its current label output and tests must keep working.

proposed_scope.summary: Delta only: add an optional second parameter to the existing render function that emits a fill attribute on the <text> element. When no fill is supplied, the output is byte-identical to today's <text>${label}</text>. No rewrite of the existing module; one function, one signature extension.
implemented_delta: src/board.js:1 — render(label) became render(label, fill); without fill the string is unchanged.
tests/fill.test.js (new) — asserts both the unchanged default output and the fill-attribute output.
package.json:1 — npm test now also runs tests/fill.test.js (the existing test file and its assertions were not edited).

key_decision_question: How should the user-selected fill value be validated or constrained before it is placed inside the fill attribute (free-form string vs. checked color syntax), since render interpolates values into SVG markup unescaped?

options.title: Free-form string passthrough
options.description: Accept any string and interpolate it into fill="..." as done now. Callers are responsible for valid colors.
options.tradeoff: Simplest and matches the existing code's style (label is also interpolated unescaped); any CSS/SVG color (named, hex, rgb()) works — but a crafted string can inject attributes or elements into the markup.
options.shows_it_works: Existing behavior: tests/board.test.js:4 still passes unchanged (✔ existing label), plus the new test rendering with '#00ff00'.
options.grounded_in: src/board.js:1 currently does fill-free interpolation with no escaping: `export const render = label => `<text>${label}</text>`;` — the delta merely extends the same convention.

options.title: Validate the value, warn on mismatch
options.description: Check the value against the syntax of a CSS color (e.g. a small parser for #hex / rgb() / named colors); return a documented warning or throw when it does not match.
options.tradeoff: Catches typos and blocks most injection, but invents a color vocabulary the codebase has not defined and risks rejecting valid SVG values.
options.shows_it_works: New tests render('#00ff00') accepted, render('<svg>') rejected with a clear error.
options.grounded_in: docs/limitation.md:1: 'Current renderer supports labels but not a user-selected fill color. Preserve its existing label output.' — the doc names the feature but says nothing about validation, so the constraint level is undecidable from the repo.

options.title: Named palette options
options.description: Restrict the selectable fill to a small fixed palette (e.g. a map of palette names to colors) instead of free strings.
options.tradeoff: Safest and easiest for users to pick, but makes 'user-selected color' narrower than the task text implies and adds a palette definition no file provides.
options.shows_it_works: Palette map present with tests covering each entry; unknown name rejected.
options.grounded_in: Task text: 'user-selected fill color' — a palette is one reading of that; no repo file defines any palette.

recommendation: The minimal passthrough (A) is already implemented and green; whether B or C is wanted is a requester decision, not something a file in this repo answers.
notes: Proposal only; nothing here is approved and no person was consulted. The existing test file tests/board.test.js and its content were left untouched.
